components.name: Input Field

components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 0.375rem; color: var(--color-text-muted); font: 560 0.75rem/1.24 var(--font-sans); letter-spacing: var(--tracking-wide); } .ds-input { min-height: 44px; border-radius: 16px; border: 1px solid rgb(var(--color-border-default-rgb) / 70%); background: var(--surface-workspace-bg); color: var(--color-text-primary); padding: 0.625rem 1rem; font: 400 0.875rem/1.56 var(--font-sans); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm), inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 14%); transition: border-color var(--motion-subtle-duration) var(--motion-subtle-ease), box-shadow var(--motion-subtle-duration) var(--motion-subtle-ease); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: rgb(var(--color-text-muted-rgb) / 80%); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgb(var(--color-accent-primary-rgb) / 14%); outline-offset: 2px; border-color: rgb(var(--color-accent-primary-rgb) / 28%); }

narrative.overview: CCR UI is a dense operational workbench with an editorial surface system: quiet shell, precise labels, warm clay accent, and structured panels that help expert users see state quickly. The interface should feel trusted during configuration, sync, command execution, and usage analysis, where unclear state can cost real local data.
keyCharacteristics: Warm clay accent used sparingly for primary action and active state.
Charcoal or high-contrast ink over neutral surfaces.
Consistent rounded product controls, usually 6px to 16px, with pill buttons where actions need strong hit targets.
Motion limited to state change, feedback, route continuity, and loading.

rules.name: The Accent Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Clay accent should occupy less than 10% of a normal screen. If it appears everywhere, nothing reads as active.

rules.name: The Legacy Branch Rule
rules.body: Do not add new purple-tech, guofeng, anime, catgirl, or NEKO color variants. Existing traces are migration debt, not optional themes.

rules.name: The Product Type Rule
rules.body: Do not use fluid hero typography inside app surfaces. Fixed rem scales serve this tool better than viewport-driven display type.

rules.name: The Structural Glass Rule
rules.body: Existing glass tokens may define shell, workspace, card, modal, and status layers. Do not add decorative glass cards for visual novelty.

dos: Do keep expert density and explicit operational scope visible.
Do use clay accent for primary action, active navigation, focus, and critical emphasis.
Do preserve light and dark contrast for body text, placeholders, labels, and status text.
Do use structural surface roles: shell, workspace, card, modal, and status.
Do keep motion between 100ms and 300ms for product state changes, with reduced-motion alternatives.
Do treat Tauri-only failures in web preview as runtime limitations when the task is not web compatibility.
donts: Don't add generic SaaS admin styling, purple or purple-blue gradients, or marketing hero patterns.
Don't add heavy Liquid Glass or glassmorphism as decoration.
Don't add guofeng, neko, anime, catgirl, or mascot-heavy variants.
Don't hide operational risk behind beginner-friendly simplification.
Don't create nested cards or identical decorative card grids.
Don't use side-stripe accent borders, gradient text, or 32px plus radii on product cards.
